content: Fluconazole is a medication prescribed to treat fungal infections, including yeast infections in various parts of the body such as the vagina, mouth, throat, esophagus, abdomen, lungs, blood, and other organs. It is also used to treat fungal meningitis, which is an infection of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. Additionally, fluconazole is prescribed to prevent yeast infections in patients undergoing chemotherapy or radiation therapy prior to a bone marrow transplant. This medication belongs to a class of antifungal drugs called triazoles, and it works by inhibiting the growth of fungi responsible for infections. Fluconazole is available in tablet form and as a liquid suspension, both of which are taken orally. It is typically administered once daily. Depending on the condition being treated, you may need to take a single dose or continue treatment for several weeks or longer. The duration of therapy is determined by your specific medical condition and your response to the medication. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take fluconazole exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. In some cases, your doctor may recommend taking a double dose on the first day of treatment. Continue taking fluconazole for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if you start feeling better. Stopping the medication prematurely may result in the recurrence of the infection. Fluconazole is sometimes used to treat severe fungal infections that originate in the lungs and spread throughout the body, as well as fungal infections of the eyes, prostate, skin, and nails. It may also be prescribed to prevent fungal infections in individuals with HIV, cancer, or those who have undergone organ transplantation. If you are considering using fluconazole for these or other conditions, discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Before starting fluconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluconazole or other antifungal medications such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, or voriconazole. Do not take fluconazole if you are also taking cisapride. Provide your doctor with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently using, as fluconazole may interact with certain drugs, including but not limited to amiodarone, warfarin, midazolam, cyclosporine, erythromycin, rifampin, and oral diabetes medications. Additionally, inform your doctor if you consume large amounts of alcohol or have a history of cancer, AIDS, irregular heartbeat, or liver, kidney, or heart disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking fluconazole, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking fluconazole. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fluconazole may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, heartburn, and changes in taste perception. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include symptoms such as severe nausea, extreme fatigue, unusual bruising or bleeding, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right abdomen, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, dark urine, pale stools, seizures, rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face or extremities, and difficulty breathing or swallowing. If you experience any severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. You or your doctor may also report adverse effects to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store fluconazole in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Discard any unused liquid medication after 14 days and properly dispose of expired or unneeded medication. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include hallucinations or extreme paranoia. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may need to monitor your response to fluconazole through specific tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of fluconazole, contact your doctor. Fluconazole is sold under the brand name Diflucan®.
